pharm: Synthetic guanine nucleoside analog that, after phosphorylation, inhibits cytomegalovirus DNA polymerase; used for serious CMV infection.
quick: Induction 5 mg/kg IV q12h x14-21d; maintenance 5 mg/kg/day
Reduce dose by CrCl; significant renal clearance
summary: Ganciclovir is an intravenous nucleoside analog antiviral for cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in immunocompromised patients and prevention of CMV disease in transplant recipients. It carries a boxed warning for hematologic toxicity (granulocytopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia), impairment of fertility, fetal toxicity, mutagenesis, and carcinogenesis. It is infused over 1 hour, requires renal dose adjustment, and demands close monitoring of blood counts.
indications: Treatment of CMV retinitis in immunocompromised patients (including AIDS)
Prevention of CMV disease in transplant recipients at risk

dosage.d: 5 mg/kg once daily 7 days/week OR 6 mg/kg once daily 5 days/week
5 mg/kg once daily 7 days/week OR 6 mg/kg once daily 5 days/week
Reduce dose and/or interval per creatinine clearance
dosage.n: Significant renal clearance; supplemental dose after hemodialysis

admin: Administer only by IV infusion over 1 hour via a vein with adequate blood flow (preferably plastic cannula)
Do not give by rapid IV push, IM, or SC (causes severe tissue irritation; toxic)
Reconstitute and dilute per label; reconstituted/diluted solution is highly alkaline
Handle as a cytotoxic/hazardous drug; use gloves and avoid skin/eye contact
Maintain adequate hydration; adjust dose for renal impairment
moa: Ganciclovir is monophosphorylated intracellularly (initially by viral protein kinase, UL97, in CMV-infected cells) and then converted by cellular kinases to ganciclovir triphosphate, which competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase and incorporates into viral DNA, terminating chain elongation and inhibiting CMV replication.

absolute: Clinically significant hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to ganciclovir or valganciclovir, or any component
relative: Pre-existing cytopenias (absolute neutrophil count <500 or platelets <25,000)
monitor: Serum drug levels not routinely needed

preg: Boxed warning: potential to cause birth defects based on animal data. Avoid in pregnancy; women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception and men should use barrier contraception during and after therapy.
lact: Do not breastfeed during ganciclovir therapy due to potential serious adverse effects in the infant.
renal: Significant renal clearance; reduce dose and/or lengthen interval based on creatinine clearance. Give after hemodialysis sessions; reduced dosing in dialysis patients.

major: Other myelosuppressive agents (zidovudine, antineoplastics) - additive bone marrow suppression
Nephrotoxic drugs (amphotericin B, cyclosporine) - reduced clearance and additive toxicity
moderate: Mycophenolate - increased levels of both drugs in renal impairment
interactions.diagnostics: Frequent CBC with differential and platelet counts; serum creatinine for dose adjustment.

monitoring: Complete blood count with differential and platelets frequently (baseline, then regularly; consider every 2 days during induction in high-risk patients)
Serum creatinine/renal function for dose adjustment
counsel: Use effective contraception during treatment - men should use condoms during and for 90 days after therapy
Report fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding, or signs of infection promptly
Regular blood tests are needed to monitor your blood counts and kidneys
Do not breastfeed while on this medicine
Keep eye appointments if treated for CMV retinitis
pk: ~3-4 hours (normal renal function); prolonged in renal impairment
Store powder at controlled room temperature; use reconstituted solution per stability guidance
pearls: Boxed warning: hematologic toxicity, impaired fertility, fetal toxicity, mutagenesis, and carcinogenesis
Neutropenia is the dose-limiting toxicity; consider G-CSF support if severe
Valganciclovir is the oral prodrug for outpatient CMV therapy/prophylaxis
Handle and dispose of as a cytotoxic agent
Renal dosing is essential - ganciclovir is largely renally cleared
missed: Administered in a clinical setting; if a scheduled infusion is delayed, give as soon as possible and adjust subsequent timing. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause severe neutropenia, pancytopenia, hepatitis, seizures, and renal toxicity. Manage with hydration, hematopoietic growth factors, and supportive care; hemodialysis reduces plasma concentrations.
